options: Its flight is purely ballistic
Its flight is partly powered
Its flight is strongly resisted
cards.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all. Its flight is purely ballistic.
cards.stem: How is the flight of a thrown ball described?

options: The only force on the ball after it leaves the hand is its weight
The only force on the ball after it leaves the hand is its drag
The only force on the ball after it leaves the hand is its spin
cards.quote: The only force on the ball after it leaves the hand is its weight, which pulls it straight down.
cards.stem: What pulls the ball down after it leaves the hand?

options: Nothing pushes the ball sideways
Something pushes the ball sideways
Gravity pushes the ball sideways
cards.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight and the ball moves x = U0 * t across the ground.
cards.stem: What happens to horizontal speed during the flight?

options: Because g on the Moon is about six times smaller
Because g on Earth is about six times smaller
Because g on the Moon is about two times smaller
cards.quote: Because g on the Moon is about six times smaller, the same throw rises about six times higher than on Earth.
cards.stem: Why does the same throw rise higher on the Moon?
